title: Colleagues
hookLine: the people at work are your neighbors
tomorrow: what does a good boss owe, and what does a worker owe back?

lines: A HOUSE TOO PACKED TO ENTER.
cards: A shift goes sideways: the oven's running hot, the line's out the door, and the new person is drowning. Mark tells about four people who once carried a load together. Their friend can't walk.
Jesus is teaching in a house in Capernaum, so packed that nobody can get near the door. So the four climb up onto the roof, open it up, and lower their friend down on his mat, one corner each.

teach.b: Feel that scene for a second. Dust and bits of roof falling on the crowd below. Rope pulling at their palms.
Four corners, four people, the weight shifting whenever one of them slips.
Then Mark's surprising line, in the Douay-Rheims: "when Jesus had seen their faith." Their faith. The carriers.
Before a word is said to the man on the mat, Jesus notices the people holding the corners. Colleagues are a lot like that. Mostly you didn't choose them.
You're in the same packed house with the same crowd at the door, and the work only moves when each one takes a corner.
Paul gives it to the Galatians as a rule for any community: "Bear ye one another's burdens; and so you shall fulfil the law of Christ."
And in Luke, when a lawyer asks Jesus who his neighbor is, the answer is a story about a traveler who stops on the road for a stranger.

teach.h: THE NEIGHBOR AT THE NEXT STATION.
teach.b: At work, the neighbor is often the person at the next station.
Here's the thing to tell a friend: in Mark, the first faith Jesus sees in this story isn't the sick man's. It's his friends'.

how: Catholics hear Galatians 6:2 read at Mass and count helping a coworker among ordinary works of love; some workplaces have Catholic groups that pray for colleagues by name.

o: the friends you'd pick to be closest to
rivals competing for the same promotion
the people you work beside, as neighbors

games.q: who carried what — tap the pairs.
p: carried the mat up to the roof

s: in Mark, Jesus first notices the sick man's own faith
Mark says Jesus saw their faith: the friends who carried him.
the friends went through the roof because the house was packed
nobody could get near the door.
Mark gives the names of the four carriers
he never names them; we only know there were four.

games.q: a coworker is buried before a deadline and you finished early. leaving on time is allowed. what would the four on the roof do?
o: ask if you can take one corner of it before you go.
leave on time; everyone carries their own load.
stay and quietly redo their work without asking.
games.why: the four each took a corner, and Jesus saw their faith. asking first keeps your coworker carrying too, just not alone.

practice: Stand and hold your arms out low, as if you had one corner of a mat, and feel the pull in your shoulders. Bring to mind one person you work or study with who's carrying something heavy right now.
Hold your corner for them until the bell, and choose one small way to lift some of it.

wordCard.voice: Colleagues. The people you work beside: neighbors, each holding a corner.

orig.note: Greek, Galatians 6:2: bear one another's burdens.

carryVoice: The line to keep: neighbors at work, each one holding a corner of the mat. That's the day, done.
